title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-jordan-lee
content:
PR: 2145 - kv-cache + continuous-batching prototype
Author: @morgan-chen
Owner: Jordan Lee (scratchpad)
Goal: Review prototype changes that introduce a KV-prefix cache and continuous batching shim for the LLM serving runtime. Quick look for perf regressions, correctness, and rollout strategy.

SUMMARY NOTES:
- High-level: Adds a per-request prefix-keyed KV cache to reuse KV cache segments across requests with same prefix. Adds a batching layer that continuously groups in-flight requests when under latency SLOs.
- Files touched: runtime/kv_cache.py, runtime/continuous_batcher.py, runtime/dispatch.py, tests/test_kv_cache.py, examples/benchmarks/kv_batch_bench.py
- Perf claim in PR: 18-30% token cost reduction for stable prefix patterns; median p95 latency impact reported ~+6ms locally.

QUICK REVIEW CHECKLIST (first pass):
- [ ] Does kv_cache.py handle eviction correctly under concurrent writes? (look at _evict_oldest, race with write_back)
- [ ] Are locks granular (per-shard) or global? currently uses a global threading.RLock in cache; consider per-prefix or per-shard locks to avoid contention
- [ ] Continuous batcher: ensure that batching timer is stopped on shutdown and does not leak goroutines/threads
- [ ] Verify compatibility with existing KV cache warmup (dedicated paths) and with model sharding (multi-GPU)
- [ ] Unit tests: tests/test_kv_cache.py covers basic hit/miss but not concurrent hammer; add stress test with 1000 concurrent requests and synthetic prefixes
- [ ] End-to-end integration test: add a smoke test in ci/integration that runs the bench with small model to verify latency SLOs
- [ ] Docs: add short note in docs/ops/kv_cache.md about config knobs: prefix_ttl, max_shards, batching_target_latency_ms

DETAILED NOTES/OBSERVATIONS:
- kv_cache.py:_evict_oldest uses OrderedDict.popitem(last=False) but there is a path that increments size and calls _maybe_evict without lock held; need to re-check ordering of lock acquisition in put() -> _maybe_evict() -> _evict_oldest(). Potential race where size becomes negative if two threads evict simultaneously.
- Suggest replacing global RLock with a small ShardMap that hashes prefix -> shard index (e.g., 64 shards) to reduce contention. This file already has a TODO comment for sharding but not implemented.
- continuous_batcher currently uses time.sleep loop with dynamic windowing; prefer using condition variables or event-driven wakeups to reduce CPU spin under low QPS.
- dispatch.py: routing logic short-circuits to fallback model when batcher returns empty batch; but path doesn't set request.metadata['fallback_reason'] which downstream logging expects. Small bug for observability.
- tests: flaky test noted in CI: tests/test_dispatch.py::test_fallback_on_empty_batch — failure due to race; add deterministic join and use event injection to simulate empty-batcher scenario.

REFactor IDEAS:
- Move cache eviction into a separate EvictionPolicy class (LRU/LFU) with clear interface to allow easier testing and swap-in of approximations (CLOCK) for large scale. Keep current simple LRU impl as default.
- Abstract BatchWindow policy from continuous_batcher into a pluggable policy so we can experiment with percentile-based windows vs fixed latency target.
- Add metrics hooks (counter/gauge) in kv_cache for hits/misses per-prefix, and batching for batch_size distribution. Expose via runtime.metrics. This is critical to validate claims in production.

MEASUREMENTS (from local bench included in PR):
- Bench command used: python examples/benchmarks/kv_batch_bench.py --qps 50 --prefix-dist zipf --duration 120s
- Observed: baseline (no cache) median tokens/sec 1200, with cache + batching median tokens/sec 1500. p95 latency baseline 38ms, with changes 44ms. Need cluster-level numbers (multi-GPU) before trusting cost claims.

FOLLOW-UPS/ACTION ITEMS (assignments):
- @morgan-chen: add stress tests for concurrency + add lock per-shard prototype (due: next week)
- @avery-kim: run CI integration bench on dedicated ci-power cluster and paste results in PR comments (INF-1234)
- Jordan Lee (me): prototype per-shard locking change in a small branch to measure contention; also add a dedicated metric for per-prefix hit-rate.
- @ravi-patel: confirm that telemetry team can ingest the new metric names (kv_cache.hits, kv_cache.misses) without backfill issues

QUESTIONS FOR AUTHOR
- What was the design rationale for global lock vs shard? was simplicity the main reason?
- Are there workloads where prefix space is huge (no reuse) — how does mem pressure look then? need fallback TTL tuning.
- How does this interact with prefix-specific quantization or model state? any security isolation concerns?

DEPLOY/ROLLOUT NOTES
- Recommend behind a kill-switch flag defaulted off. Gradual rollout: 10% of traffic (canary), then 50%, 100% if metrics stable. Watch: p95 latency, median latency, token cost, error rate.
- Add guardrail that disables cache if per-prefix hit-rate < 5% over 5m window to avoid wasted memory and added latency.

SNIPPETS/PATCH POINTERS
- runtime/kv_cache.py line ~220: wrap _maybe_evict call with same lock as put() (currently it calls without acquiring)
- runtime/continuous_batcher.py line ~85: replace busy sleep with Condition wait; also ensure self._stop_event is checked inside wait predicate

NOTES TO SELF (todo):
- Write quick repro script for the race by hammering put() and evict in parallel (use multiprocessing to get real concurrency)
- Draft a short Confluence page summarizing perf tradeoffs and rollout plan (link to here)

END

-- Jordan
